```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

OccurrenceCleaner is an extension of CoordinateCleaner (Zizka et al. [2019](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13152)) tailored to large-scale occurrence data. It flags errors in species occurrence records and keeps every record. Each test sets one bit in an integer flag word, so deciding which records to drop is a query over the flags, made after the pass and changed without rerunning it.

## Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/OccurrenceCleaner")
```

Needs a C++ compiler (Rtools on Windows).

```{r setup}
library(OccurrenceCleaner)
```

## Flag a data frame

The input needs longitude, latitude and a species column under their Darwin Core names (`decimalLongitude`, `decimalLatitude`, `species`; matching is case-insensitive, and `occ_columns()` renames them).

```{r}
x <- data.frame(
  species = c("Quercus robur", "Quercus robur", "Fagus sylvatica", "Fagus sylvatica", "Pinus nigra"),
  decimalLongitude = c(12.58, 0, 16.37, 16.37, -30),
  decimalLatitude = c(55.67, 0, 48.21, 48.21, 40),
  countryCode = c("DK", NA, "AT", "AT", "FR")
)
f <- flag_occurrences(x, tests = c("invalid", "zero", "capital", "gbif_headquarters", "sea",
                                  "country_mismatch", "duplicate"))
knitr::kable(f[, c("species", "flags", "flag_zero", "flag_capital", "flag_gbif_headquarters",
                   "flag_sea", "flag_country_mismatch", "flag_duplicate")])
```

The first record is within 1 km of the GBIF headquarters in Copenhagen, hence also within 10 km of a capital; it also fails `country_mismatch`, because that point lies just off the 1:50m Natural Earth coastline of Denmark. The second is a zero coordinate at sea with no country code. The third and fourth are the same species at the same place in Vienna, so the fourth is a duplicate; both are in a capital. The fifth is in the Atlantic with a French country code.

## The tests

```{r}
knitr::kable(flag_tests()[, c("bit", "test", "definition", "equivalent")])
```

The tests with an `equivalent` are CoordinateCleaner's record tests with its default buffers, up to the differences listed in the article Coming from CoordinateCleaner; the others read GBIF's `issue`, `basisOfRecord` and `establishmentMeans` fields. `default_tests()` names the tests that need only coordinates and a species.

## Rules are queries over the flags

A rule is a set of tests. `has_flag()` marks the records any of them flags:

```{r}
strict <- c("zero", "capital", "gbif_headquarters", "sea", "duplicate")
mild <- c("zero", "sea")
knitr::kable(data.frame(species = f$species, strict = has_flag(f$flags, strict), mild = has_flag(f$flags, mild)))
```

`tally_flags()` counts, per group, how many records each test flags and how many each rule removes. It returns one `flagged_<test>` column per test; a few are shown here:

```{r}
t <- tally_flags(f, by = "species", rules = list(strict = strict, mild = mild))
knitr::kable(t[, c("species", "n", "flagged_capital", "flagged_sea", "flagged_duplicate",
                   "removed_strict", "removed_mild")])
```

Numeric columns such as the record year or the stated coordinate uncertainty stay raw and are cut at tally time:

```{r}
f$year <- c(1890, 1950, 1999, 2015, NA)
t <- tally_flags(f, bins = list(year = c(1950, 2000)), rules = list(strict = strict))
knitr::kable(t[, c("year_bin", "n", "removed_strict", "kept_strict")])
```

## Buffers, reference data and scale

The buffers default to CoordinateCleaner's (10 km capitals, 1 km centroids, 100 m institutions, 1 km GBIF headquarters, 0.5 degrees around the origin) and can be changed per test:

```{r}
flag_occurrences(x[3, ], tests = "capital")$flag_capital
flag_occurrences(x[3, ], tests = "capital", buffers = list(capital = 500))$flag_capital
```

The gazetteers are rebuilt from Natural Earth and GBIF's registry of scientific collections, each pinned to a version and checksum:

```{r}
knitr::kable(reference_info()[, c("layer", "source", "version", "retrieved")])
```

`reference = "CoordinateCleaner"` uses that package's own tables instead, which gives its flags up to the same differences (CoordinateCleaner must be installed). The land layer for the `sea` test comes at Natural Earth scale 110 (the default of CoordinateCleaner's `cc_sea()`; its `clean_coordinates()` uses 50), 50, or 10; the 1:10m layer is downloaded once on first use.

## A table on disk

The same verb streams an on-disk table through vectra: a directory of Parquet parts such as a GBIF snapshot, a `.vtr` file, or a delimited file. Each input file is one unit of work; the flags are written as `.vtr` parts next to the columns kept for grouping, and a rerun skips finished units.

```{r}
src <- tempfile("records"); dir.create(src)
set.seed(1)
big <- data.frame(gbifID = as.character(1:5000), kingdom = sample(c("Animalia", "Plantae"), 5000, TRUE),
                  year = sample(1900:2020, 5000, TRUE), species = sample(letters, 5000, TRUE),
                  decimalLongitude = runif(5000, -180, 180), decimalLatitude = runif(5000, -60, 70))
vectra::write_vtr(big[1:2500, ], file.path(src, "part-1.vtr"))
vectra::write_vtr(big[2501:5000, ], file.path(src, "part-2.vtr"))

out <- flag_occurrences(src, out = tempfile("flags"), keep = c("kingdom", "year"), verbose = FALSE)
out
t <- tally_flags(out, by = "kingdom", bins = list(year = c(1950, 2000)),
                 rules = list(cc = c("zero", "equal", "capital", "centroid", "institution",
                                     "gbif_headquarters", "sea")))
knitr::kable(t[, c("kingdom", "year_bin", "n", "flagged_sea", "flagged_capital", "removed_cc", "kept_cc")])
```

For a GBIF snapshot, point `flag_occurrences()` at the `occurrence.parquet` directory and pass the taxon, year and uncertainty columns through `keep`. `flagged_table()` opens the output as a vectra table for anything the tally does not cover.
